evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna: 'might need about ten to fifteen minutes to discuss your move... that's fine'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Joanna: 'before we start just wanted to check-in if you have any important concerns or instructions for this move that you also want to discuss on this call' — asked before any logistics probing
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised TV mounting concern; Joanna followed up: 'We can definitely help you this mount then, but we just cannot mount and mount them on your new home' — addressed the concern and clarified the boundary
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna: 'for now since we have those additional items...I'll just put you more on the seven and a half to eight and a half hour mark. Which would be an estimated budget of $2,117' — anchored to typical three-bedroom move, personalized to added beds and distance change
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Joanna: '$111 per hour per mover...includes the you guys and the truck, and all the reps to protect your furniture...travel fee of $230...two and a half hour minimum...every fifteen minute increments' — trip fee and minimum disclosed, 15-min increment framing included
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Joanna: 'would you like us to go ahead and help you with this move so we can get you on the schedule already?' — plain ask, no out

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details systematically (property type, floors, room count, garage items, parking distance, fragile goods, furniture count) and tied the estimate directly to what the customer actually had to move, making the $2,117 anchor credible and personalized.
coaching_note: After the estimate is given, pause and ask 'Does that feel fair?' — do not skip straight to the explicit ask without checking for price objections first; also in Section 6, ask a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' instead of the throwaway 'Any other questions?' to surface last-minute worries before closing.
